tensions: Every exit rule in v5.7.22 is currently inert. No thesis broken, no -15% stop, no 21-day dead money, no position over 25%. So the system has nothing to say about a book that is up 71% and fully invested in extended names. That is the gap: the ruleset is built to stop bad selling, and it has succeeded, but it offers no discipline at all on entries. The churn is happening on the buy side and in same-day reversals that the 7-day hold was supposed to prevent and did not. Second tension: AAVE is the disciplined, boring, revenue-backed pick, and it will probably underperform NEAR or SUI if this altseason has another leg. Buying the laggard is right on process and may well be wrong on outcome for the next three weeks. Third: $105 left in cash is either prudence or indecision, and the honest answer is that there was no second idea worth 0.95%.

opening.text: Book is $2,112 against $1,231 deposited, up 71.6%. Every position is green, which is less a compliment to the selection than a description of the tape: BTC dominance broke below 60% and alts are running. NEAR +61% on our basis, LTC +37%, ONDO +37%, W +34%. Enjoy it and do not confuse a rising tide with skill.

Three things the scan prompt got wrong. Cash is $304.64, not $17.43, so 14.4% of the book sat idle through the best alt week of the quarter. AVAX 9.0511 (about $100) sits in the account with zero order history behind it; it is not in the prompt table and nothing in this account bought it. And the position table is five trades stale. Fix the source of truth before trusting another signal from it.

The real damage is not a bad pick, it is friction. Sep 21 to 26 cost $15.10 in fees on a $2.1k book, 0.7% in six days, roughly 37% annualized. The SUI round trip on Sep 25 is the indictment: bought 166.7 at $1.188, sold two and a half hours later at $1.169, lost $6.82, then watched SUI run 50% on the week. That trade broke the 7-day minimum hold and paid for the privilege. The fee tier also slipped from 0.75% to 0.95% taker, so a round trip is now 1.9% before spread. The 3% net hurdle in v5.7.22 is too generous. Make it 4%.

One order today: buy $200 AAVE at about $154.79, roughly 1.2799 AAVE, $1.90 fee, pre-validated. Aave V3 leads all lending by fees at $35.6M over 30 days and is accelerating 8.2% week over week, while AAVE the token is up only 14% on the week, the least extended major on the screen. Not chasing the BCH CME squeeze, not re-entering SUI, not rotating to BTC or ETH because the dominance check fails on its second condition: BTC is underperforming the median alt. Keep the last $105 in cash. Doing nothing is a position.
